title: AI refutes 30-year-old mathematical assumption in computer science | New Scientist
description: A central tenet in computer science has apparently been disproven by OpenAI, a result that will force textbooks to be rewritten if it is confirmed
author: Chris Stokel-Walker

title: Clues from the Dead Sea could explain ancient drying of the Mediterranean | New Scientist
description: The high salt concentration in the Dead Sea drives the warming and shrinking of the lake, and something similar may have happened in the Mediterranean 5.5 million years ago
author: Bas den Hond

title: Major greenhouse gases rise again to record levels | New Scientist
description: Levels of carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide in the atmosphere continued to rise in 2025, along with a lesser-known gas with a more powerful warming effect
author: Shosha Adie

title: Wind turbines have killed 19 million bats in 40 years in the US | New Scientist
description: Nearly 19 million bats are estimated to have been killed by wind turbines in the US between 1981 and 2024, but measures can be taken to make them less deadly
author: Christa Lesté-Lasserre

title: 'Oddball' test lets us glimpse how monkeys see the world | New Scientist
description: Compared with humans, macaques are more likely to miss the bigger picture, but are also less confused by flipped images
author: Jo Marchant

title: Predatory amphibians swam the seas 237 million years ago | New Scientist
description: Until now, it was thought that the squishy, permeable skin of amphibians was unsuited for marine life because it would absorb too much salt from sea water – but a fossil found in China upends that view
author: James Woodford
